privacy.title: How Akhra uses your information
privacy.intro: A plain summary of what the platform does with the details you give it. It describes how the software works today; it is not a legal policy.
privacy.collectBody: To report a problem: your name, mobile number, district and the details of the problem. To create an account: your name and email address, or your Google account.
privacy.passwordBody: Sign-in is handled by Clerk, a specialist identity service. Akhra never sees or stores your password; Clerk keeps it hashed and checks new passwords against known data breaches.
privacy.emailBody: Sign-in and password-reset codes (sent by Clerk), and updates about reports you made. Nothing else.
privacy.purposeBody: Your name and mobile number let the district officer and the team working on your report reach you, and let you prove a report is yours when you track it. Your district decides which officer it goes to. Nothing you give is used for advertising, sold, or shared outside the departments and institutions working on your report.
privacy.keepBody: A report and its timeline stay on the platform as the public record of what was raised and what was done — that record is the point of the service. Your contact details stay while the report is open and for one year after it closes, so the department can be asked about it. Sign-in details are kept by Clerk while your account exists, and removed when you delete it.
privacy.rightsTitle: What you can do with your information
privacy.rightsBody: Signed in, the Account page shows the details Akhra holds about you, lets you correct them, and lets you sign out of every device at once. To have your contact details removed from a report, or to get a copy of what is held about you, file a request on Akhra as described below and quote your reference code.
privacy.contactBody: Akhra is a prototype built for Smart India Hackathon; it is not yet operated by any government body. It is designed to be run by a state department, which would then be responsible for the information it holds and would name the Grievance Officer required by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 here. Until then, raise a question or a complaint about your information on Akhra itself, under “Public Administration & Service Delivery”: it gets a reference code and is answered like any other report.
privacy.shown1: The title and description of a report, its district and its category.
privacy.shown2: Its reference code and every public step on its timeline, with the officers and teams who took them.
privacy.shown3: The public updates the team working on it posts in the report’s conversation.
privacy.hidden1: Your name, mobile number and email address.
privacy.hidden2: Photos, videos and documents you attach. Only the district officer and the team working on the report can open them.
privacy.hidden3: Internal notes between officers, institutions and partners.

landing.titleLine2: Follow it until it is solved.
landing.intro: Tell Akhra what is wrong in your area. Your district officer sends it to the department that can fix it, or to a university team that can find a lasting solution. You can follow every step, and the report closes only when you say it is fixed.
landing.sampleData: Sample data: these figures come from demonstration records, not real reports.
landing.stepReportBody: Describe the problem, add a photo if you can, and mark the place. No account needed.
landing.stepSortBody: Akhra suggests a category and checks for the same problem reported by others.
landing.stepDecideBody: Your district officer checks it and sends it to a department (21 days) or a university team.
landing.stepSolveBody: The department fixes it, or a university team, with industry support, builds and tests a solution.
landing.stepCloseBody: You confirm it is fixed, or reopen it within 30 days.
landing.reportForOffice: Report a problem on behalf of your office

how.title: How Akhra works
how.intro: Every report follows a public path. Here is each step, who takes it, and how long it should take.
how.reportedBody: Describe the problem, choose the district, and add a photo and a pin on the map if you can. Akhra suggests a category and checks whether someone has already reported the same thing.
how.validatedBody: Within 3 days the officer confirms the report, moves it to the right district if needed, or joins it to an earlier report of the same problem. After that, it takes one of two paths.
how.routedBody: Institutions are ranked on their expertise, faculty, facilities and distance, and the officer sees why.
how.collaborateBody: Students and a faculty mentor write a proposal with milestones. The district officer approves it before work starts.
how.pilotedTitle: Built and tested in the field
how.pilotedBody: Industry partners, startups and CSR programmes can offer funding, mentoring, labs or deployment. Every test, including failures, is recorded.
how.deployedBody: The solution is deployed and its results are recorded: households served, patents filed, policies changed.
how.aiBody: An AI model suggests the category. If it is unavailable, an offline model that reads English and Hindi takes over, so reporting never stops. The district officer always confirms it.
how.ctaTitle: Seen a problem in your area?
how.ctaBody: Reporting takes about five minutes, and you do not need an account.
how.firstTitle: Every report starts the same way
how.firstBody: You do not need an account. Keep the reference code you are given: it is how you follow the report.
how.departmentBody: For something broken that a department can repair, such as a handpump, a road or a streetlight.
how.assignedBody: The department has 21 days, and must post an update if it needs more than 14.
how.actionTakenTitle: The department records what it did
how.actionTakenBody: You see its note on your report’s page.
how.confirmedTitle: You decide if it is fixed
how.confirmedBody: Confirm and the report closes. If it is not fixed, reopen it once within 30 days and it goes back to the department with a new 21-day deadline.
how.researchBody: For a problem that has no ready fix, such as contaminated groundwater or crop disease across a block.

resources.title: Resources
resources.intro: How to write a report that gets acted on, and answers to common questions.
resources.reportTitle: How to write a good report
resources.reportBody: A clear report reaches the right people faster.
resources.q1Question: Do I need an account to report a problem?
resources.q1Answer: No. You can report without an account; keep the reference code to follow it. An account lets you see all your reports in one place.
resources.q2Answer: Yes. Every page works in English and Hindi, and reports written in Hindi are classified just as well.
resources.q3Question: How does my report reach the right people?
resources.q3Answer: Akhra suggests a category and your district officer checks it. From there it goes one of two ways: to the department that can fix it directly, or — when it needs something new built — to the universities ranked highest for that subject and nearest to you. Your tracker shows where it went.
resources.q4Answer: No. Your mobile number and email address are never shown on public pages.
resources.q5Question: How can my university or company join?
resources.q5Answer: Through an agreement with the state department that runs Akhra. The state then sends your administrator an invitation, and your administrator invites colleagues.
resources.q6Question: Can I see what is actually being done?
resources.q6Answer: Yes. Once a district officer approves the team’s proposal, your tracker shows it in full: what they plan to build, how, the steps they set themselves, every test they ran — including the ones that failed — and what finally changed.
resources.q7Question: What happens when the department says it is fixed?
resources.q7Answer: You do, not them. The report waits on your answer: confirm it and it closes, or say what is still wrong and it reopens with your words attached. Nobody can close a report over your head.
resources.tip1: Say what is wrong and where: the village, ward or landmark.
resources.tip2: Say since when, and how many people it affects.
resources.tip3: Add a clear photo and drop a pin on the map if you can.
resources.tip4: Tick the safety box if anyone is at risk, so it is looked at first.
resources.q8Question: What if someone already reported the same problem?
resources.q8Answer: Your district officer joins the two into one case. You keep your own reference code, your report shows which one it joined, and you get every update on it.
resources.q9Question: I lost my reference code. What can I do?
resources.q9Answer: If you gave an email address, the code is in the confirmation email. If you reported while signed in, it is under My reports. Otherwise it cannot be recovered, so note it down when you report.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: Akhra is for everyone in Jharkhand, including people who use a screen reader, a keyboard alone, a magnifier, or a slow connection on a small phone. This page says what has been built for that, what has not, and how to tell us when something blocks you.
accessibility.standardBody: Level AA of IS 17802 (Part 1), India’s accessibility standard for ICT products, which adopts WCAG 2.1 Level AA. This is the level the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW 3.0) and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 expect of a public service.
accessibility.done1: Every page works in English and Hindi, and the page declares its language so a screen reader pronounces it correctly.
accessibility.done2: Everything can be reached and operated with a keyboard alone, and whatever has focus is visibly outlined.
accessibility.done3: A “Skip to content” link is the first thing a keyboard or screen reader reaches on every page.
accessibility.done4: Every button, link and form control is at least 44 pixels tall, so it can be hit without fine motor control.
accessibility.done5: Every colour pair used for text is checked against the AA contrast ratio automatically, and a change that falls below it fails the build.
accessibility.done6: Nothing is explained by colour alone: a status is a word, a chart has its numbers written beside it, and the district map has a table view.
accessibility.done7: Forms name their fields, mark what is required and say what went wrong in words, next to the field.
accessibility.done8: The report form needs only a district from a list; dropping a pin on the map is optional and adds precision.
accessibility.limitsBody: Stated plainly, because a statement that claims everything is a statement nobody can rely on.
accessibility.limit1: Akhra has not been audited by an independent agency, and holds no STQC Certified Quality Website certificate. Everything above is our own assessment.
accessibility.limit2: It has not been tested end to end with NVDA, JAWS or TalkBack by people who use them daily.
accessibility.limit3: The map used to drop a pin on a report needs a pointer or touch. The district list beside it is the accessible route, and it is the field that is actually required.
accessibility.limit4: Files that people upload to a report — photographs, scanned letters — carry no text description, so a screen reader cannot convey what they show.
accessibility.feedbackBody: Tell us the same way you would report anything else in Jharkhand: file it on Akhra under “Accessibility & Inclusion”, and say which page and what stopped you. It gets a reference code and is answered like any other report — you can follow it the whole way.
accessibility.reviewed: Self-assessed and last reviewed in September 2026.
